name: Video-MME
description: Video-MME is the first-ever comprehensive Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark for MLLMs in Video analysis. The dataset comprises 900 videos across 6 primary visual domains with 30 subfields, spanning short (11 seconds), medium (4-15 minutes), and long (30-60 minutes) durations. It includes 2,700 high-quality multiple-choice questions (3 per video) with manual expert annotations, along with associated subtitles (744 videos) and audio tracks (900 videos) to enable comprehensive multimodal assessment.
creator: Chaoyou Fu, Yuhan Dai, Yongdong Luo, Lei Li, Shuhuai Ren, Renrui Zhang, Zihan Wang, Chenyu Zhou, Yunhang Shen, Mengdan Zhang, Peixian Chen, Yanwei Li, Shaohui Lin, Sirui Zhao, Ke Li, Tong Xu, Xiawu Zheng, Enhong Chen, Caifeng Shan, Ran He, Xing Sun
citeAs: Chaoyou Fu et al. Video-MME: The First-Ever Comprehensive Evaluation Benchmark of Multi-modal LLMs in Video Analysis. arXiv:2405.21075v3, 2025.
rai:dataCollection: Videos were collected from YouTube across 6 key domains (Knowledge, Film & Television, Sports Competition, Artistic Performance, Life Record, and Multilingual) with 30 fine-grained categories. For each category, videos with varying duration lengths were collected, including short (<2 minutes), medium (4-15 minutes), and long videos (30-60 minutes). Meta-information such as subtitles and audios were also obtained.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw videos were sourced from YouTube based on a domain hierarchy covering 6 key domains with 30 specific tags/categories. The dataset consists of 900 videos, including 744 videos with subtitles and all 900 with audios.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Frame extraction was performed from videos. For Gemini 1.5 Pro, frames were sampled at 1 frame per second for short and medium videos, and at 1 frame every 2 seconds for long videos. For other models, frame extraction followed their respective official guidelines, uniformly sampling a specified number of frames from the video. In the subtitle-enabled setting, subtitles corresponding to the timestamps of the sampled video frames were selected.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Expert annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning were recruited. Each annotator thoroughly viewed the entire video, then iteratively created three relevant questions, each accompanied by four candidate options. Questions encompass 12 distinct task types, including perception, reasoning, and information synthesis. Each QA pair was designed to be closely tied to the video content, preventing MLLMs from answering accurately without directly referencing the video.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each QA pair underwent examination by a different annotator to verify that: (i) the language expression is clear and precise; (ii) the question is answerable with logically consistent candidate options, and the designated correct answer is appropriate. To ensure questions are sufficiently challenging and require video content as a critical clue, text-only questions were provided to Gemini 1.5 Pro to filter out QA pairs that can be answered solely based on textual questions. Questions not meeting this criterion were returned to the original annotator for revision. Statistical analysis shows that Gemini 1.5 Pro achieves less than 15% accuracy in the text-only setup.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Annotators with strong English proficiency and extensive research experience in vision-language learning.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Gemini 1.5 Pro was used during the quality review process to filter out QA pairs that could be answered solely based on textual questions without video content.
rai:dataLimitations: A general decline in MLLM performance is observed as video duration increases for all models. For open-source models, the restricted input frames can become an information bottleneck for understanding the full content of long videos. The long-tailed distribution of complex temporal reasoning data poses challenges for acquisition. Current limitations in processing longer video sequences could be a critical bottleneck in the performance of MLLMs.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating and benchmarking MLLMs on video understanding tasks. It can be used for testing both video-specific MLLMs and image-based MLLMs by extending their input to multi-frame images. The benchmark enables comprehensive evaluation of temporal understanding, perception capabilities, reasoning abilities, and multimodal integration (video frames, subtitles, audio) across varying video durations.
